A1.justification: Both complete 26-page PDFs describe the same SpeechEval dataset and SQ-LLM study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on four speech evaluation tasks, multilingual performance, and CoT/GRPO ablations in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds expert-baseline comparisons, human-rated ablations, and source-specific deepfake detection results.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-Omni-based architecture, frozen speech encoder, LoRA adaptation, dimension-wise CoT supervision, joint loss, GRPO rewards, and task prompts remain unchanged. Expanded documentation does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use SpeechEval's 32,207 utterances and 128,754 annotations across the same four languages and four tasks. The human evaluation and source-specific detection breakdown examine retained task and data coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds MOSNet, UTMOS, and AudioBox Aesthetics as standalone expert comparators for assessment and comparison, introducing a substantial comparison family absent from those experiments in v1. The AudioBox-based LLM pipeline is retained under the clarified name Qwen2.5-7B + AES-E.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 introduces human evaluation with eight raters, 60 instances per model, at least three ratings per instance, and a 1–5 scale. BLEU-4, METEOR, ROUGE-L, and CIDEr-D are dropped from the reported evaluation. Section 5.1 also removes the early-stopping statement for SQ-LLM; this does not establish that training was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds human-rated CoT/GRPO ablations across three generation tasks (Figure 7) and a language-by-source analysis of deepfake detection failures (Appendix D, Table 14). These substantially extend the existing automatic ablations. The comparison heatmap redisplays v1 Table 15 rather than constituting a new analysis.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 7 introduces 95% item-level bootstrap confidence intervals for the human-rated ablation. This uncertainty reporting is localized to the new study; benchmark tables remain point estimates, and neither version reports training seed counts or repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds expert-baseline scores, human ratings, and source-specific detection outcomes, while removing four automatic-metric series and the comparison average-accuracy column. Existing SQ-LLM scores also change: assessment LScore 6.858 to 6.833, comparison LScore 6.420 to 6.434, and speech-rate accuracy 0.726 to 0.731. Appendix Table 13 corrects average PCC from 0.476 to 0.459 while retaining the seven component correlations.

T1.justification: The joint training objective and reward definitions in Equations (1)–(3) are unchanged. No new or revised theoretical assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: a multilingual multitask dataset, a CoT/GRPO-trained evaluator, and interpretable, generalizable speech quality evaluation. The new experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly interprets detection failures as difficulty generalizing to particular synthesis pipelines. Section 6 adds discussion of difficult quality dimensions and correctly emphasizes suggestions as the largest GRPO benefit, replacing v1's emphasis on detection. The formal Limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 replaces a future-release promise with a statement of public code, model, and data availability plus a repository link. It adds 43 A100 GPU-hours of training cost and detailed information about 56 annotators, qualifications, demographics, adjudication, and quality checks. These are new disclosures, not demonstrated procedural changes. Conversely, renaming Appendix B.4 removes its explicit Qwen3-8B reward-evaluator identification.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Yang et al. (2025c), Towards Responsible Evaluation for Text-to-Speech, and Zhang et al. (2025), SpeechJudge. It expands discussion of expert quality predictors and removes references associated with the four omitted metrics. The broad research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Related-work, evaluation, results, and annotation-protocol paragraphs receive localized rewrites and clearer organization. Author affiliation and correspondence information are expanded, an acknowledgement is added, and Appendix B.4 is retitled. The main section and appendix structure is retained.

P2.justification: The results presentation is substantially reorganized: v1 Tables 4–6 become a consolidated cross-task table, and Appendix Table 15 becomes a main-text heatmap. v2 adds an expert-comparison table, a human-rating plot with confidence intervals, and a source-breakdown table. The multilingual plot's accuracy axis is rescaled, alongside float and caption adjustments.

improvement.justification: Expert comparisons, direct human-rated ablations with confidence intervals, and source-specific failure analysis strengthen validation and interpretation. The corrected average PCC and additional annotation, compute, and access information improve transparency. The gain remains limited: the human study samples 60 instances per model, the added expert comparisons lack detailed protocol documentation, and four automatic metrics are no longer reported. Overall, v2 provides useful additional support for an otherwise stable study.
